title: LMCache multiprocess transport deserializes unauthenticated messages into code execution
summary: An unauthenticated message to the multiprocess ZeroMQ transport can execute code through pickle deserialization of device descriptors. The process account determines privileges.

severity.rationale: Remote code execution requires multiprocess mode bound to a reachable address, a documented multi-node configuration. That common prerequisite warrants 72 hours; default loopback-only and in-process configurations reduce network reach.

affected.note: Also affects 0.5.6rc1 through rc3. Final 0.5.6 replaces device IPC descriptor pickle serialization.

exposure: Requires access to the MP transport, which defaults to loopback but can be bound to a routable address. In-process vLLM use does not open this port. The device-descriptor fix does not remove every other pickle path or add RPC authentication.

params.instructions: Check LMCache 0.5.6 release candidates through rc3 and pre-fix development builds, and whether the MP transport is reachable by untrusted peers.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade MP servers and workers together to final 0.5.6 or later; the descriptor wire format is incompatible with older peers. Restrict MP traffic to trusted peers. Treat formerly untrusted-network-reachable vulnerable deployments as potentially compromised and redeploy clean images.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and the component used by running processes meet the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
